Let’s dive into Chapter 10: The Human Side of Innovation—Empathy, Curiosity, and Purpose.
You know, at the heart of the jobs framework is the idea that customers aren’t just numbers or anonymous market segments—they’re real people, with unique stories, hopes, and frustrations.
That means building a culture where empathy is front and center. It starts with listening—really listening—to your customers. Not just for what they say, but for what they feel and what drives their choices.
So, how do you actually nurture this mindset? Well, it’s more practical than you might think.
Imagine inviting customers to share their stories with your team—sometimes in person, sometimes through video. Suddenly, those customer personas come alive, and you start to see things from a whole new angle.
Another approach is the classic “day in the life” exercise. What if your team shadowed real customers, or even tried using your own product out in the wild? You’d be amazed at what you notice—the little frustrations, the unexpected workarounds, and moments of delight. All those details matter.
And don’t forget the emotional and social sides of every job. Sure, the functional tasks are important, but what about how your product makes someone feel? Or how it shapes their identity in a group? Taking time to reflect on those layers makes all the difference.
When you put people first, you don’t just create better solutions—you spark a sense of shared purpose within your organization. There’s something special about knowing your work is genuinely helping others move forward. That’s what boosts motivation and gets creativity flowing.
Here’s a great example: Imagine a healthcare provider who realized that patients weren’t just coming for treatment—they were looking for reassurance and hope. So, they redesigned waiting rooms to feel more comforting, trained staff to communicate with greater empathy, and improved follow-up care to give patients a sense of being truly cared for.
The results? Happier patients, better outcomes, and a team that felt more inspired than ever.
So, the big takeaway here? Innovation isn’t just about new features or clever tech—it’s about staying curious, caring deeply, and always remembering the human story behind every job to be done.
